args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with a 0.2% error rate. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression and work out why it was promoted from an unhealthy staging build.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer. The service is healthy again.

- **Cause:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0. The service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure and the rollback. It also says the v2.3.1 test build was already unhealthy in staging before release. The follow-ups it lists are finding what broke in v2.3.1 and why it went to production anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
